stances.claim: Before the PCGG is abolished, dissolved, or merged, Congress should first require it to pinpoint, locate, and account for all recovered ill-gotten assets — cash, bonds, real estate, shares, paintings, jewelry — wherever situated.
stances.evidence: Inquirer 7/27/17 report (P170B recovered, fraction of $10B initial estimate); reports of wastage, malversation, and thievery that 'must be verified and put to rest'

stances.claim: The PCGG's historical achievement — being the first body to crack Swiss banking secrecy and prevail in Swiss, US, and PH courts — is real and internationally recognized, but does not exempt it from accountability before any institutional realignment.
stances.evidence: Historical record of PCGG asset-recovery in three jurisdictions

stances.claim: FLP scholarships and dissertation prizes are concrete vehicles for advancing the philosophy of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law in the next generation of Filipino lawyers.
stances.evidence: Detailed terms, partners (Tan Yan Kee Foundation, Ayala Group, Philippine Association of Law Schools), and judging rubrics

notable_anecdotes: The PCGG was created by 'the very first executive order' of President Corazon Aquino's revolutionary government in 1986 — a foundational data-point used to underline both its historical pedigree and the gravity of any move to abolish it.

The international plaudits for the PCGG as the first body in history to crack Swiss and other 'impregnable financial havens' — set against the irony that recovered assets are now plagued by reports of wastage and malversation.
The P170 billion recovered as 'only a fraction' of the initial $10 billion estimate (P500B), excluding interest and appreciation — used to argue that the recovery story is still unfinished.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with Budget Secretary Benjamin E. Diokno's disclosure of a pending 'Rightsizing the National Government Act of 2017' bill that would abolish the PCGG and transfer its functions to the DOJ (Speaker Alvarez's parallel bill would route them through the OSG and OGCC). Before any such abolition, he argues, the PCGG should be required to pinpoint, locate, and account for every recovered ill-gotten asset -- Inquirer (July 27, 2017) reported P170 billion recovered, only a fraction of the initial $10 billion ($500B-equivalent) estimate, and reports of wastage, malversation, and outright thievery deserve verification. He honors the PCGG's pedigree as the very first executive order of Corazon Aquino's revolutionary government in 1986 and its historic role in cracking Swiss banking secrecy across three jurisdictions, but insists accountability precedes restructuring. The column then pivots to two FLP service announcements: sixteen new law scholarships for SY 2017-2018 (six senior, ten junior), co-sponsored with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation and the Philippine Association of Law Schools -- P200,000 per scholar (P100,000 tuition, P80,000 stipend, P20,000 books), with top-20 rank, ≥85% GPA, no dropped subjects, no grade below 75%, and an essay on the philosophy of liberty and prosperity due August 15; and a dissertation contest co-sponsored with the Ayala Group -- P300,000 best, P200,000 second, P100,000 each for three third-placers, plus P20,000 elimination-round prizes for the top 20, with deadline extended to September 15 -- judged on significance, comprehensiveness, innovation, and literary style. Scholarships are limited to schools above the national-mean bar-passing rate; the dissertation contest is open to all law schools.
